title: Expected contract for a resource's legacy name alias (GET/UPDATE/CREATE/DELETE)
answers: How should a resource alias behave on create/update/delete?
What tests cover the default routing tree alias?
Is creating a resource via its alias allowed?
Does deleting via an alias delete or reset the resource?
body: When a resource supports a legacy alias for a canonical name (e.g. routing tree's default/root route addressable as both the canonical name and 'user-defined'), the expected behavior exercised by integration tests is: GET/UPDATE via the alias behave identically to using the canonical name and echo the alias back as ObjectMeta.Name; CREATE via the alias is rejected (aliases can't create new resources); DELETE via the alias resets the resource to default rather than deleting it. See TestIntegrationMultipleRoutesCRUD/Default routing tree alias for the reference test pattern when adding or verifying alias support on another resource.
applies: pkg/tests/apis/alerting/notifications/routingtree integration tests, and any future resource adding alias support
says: Deleting a routing tree by its legacy alias removes it instead of resetting
Getting a routing tree by old and new names produces different results
Updating routing tree via legacy alias doesn't return the alias in the response
Creating a routing tree resource using its legacy alias name unexpectedly succeeds
Operations on routing tree via legacy alias don't match operations via canonical name
search: Resources with legacy name aliases (e.g., routing tree's 'default' or 'root' route) follow a specific CRUD contract: GET and UPDATE via the alias behave identically to the canonical name and echo the alias back as ObjectMeta.Name; CREATE via the alias is rejected because aliases cannot create new resources; DELETE via the alias resets the resource to default rather than deleting it. Reference implementation tested in pkg/tests/apis/alerting/notifications/routingtree/routing_tree_test.go:TestIntegrationMultipleRoutesCRUD. Applies to any resource implementing legacy alias support to verify contract compliance during integration testing.
